required_interface.proper-closed-convex: g_i is proper, closed by closed epigraph, and convex; domain points are finite; no hidden sequential-closedness implication is imported.
required_interface.proximal-map: for each M_i>0, completing the square uses t=1/M_i and the set-valued proximal map of the proper closed convex block penalty.
required_interface.proximal-existence: the actual theorem proves a unique proximal minimizer for every proper closed convex input and positive parameter; the local use has t=1/M_i.
required_interface.epsilon-subdifferential: the convex subgradient is ∂_0; the local block-stationarity lemma uses its all-z inequality at finite F(x).
required_interface.smooth-composite-sum: a finite continuous convex f added to proper closed convex g remains proper, closed, and convex.
required_interface.affine-minorant: a proper closed convex g on finite-dimensional Euclidean space has an affine minorant; the supplied proof uses the finite-dimensional nearest-point route.

supplier_item_records.excerpt:
def-extended-real-epsilon-subdifferential, Definition: “Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex in the convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}g$ and $\eta\ge0$, define
$$\partial_\eta g(x)=\{p\in\mathbb R^n:g(z)\ge g(x)+\langle p,z-x\rangle-\eta\text{ for every }z\in\mathbb R^n\}.$$
Write $\partial g(x)=\partial_0g(x)$. If $x\notin\operatorname{dom}g$, set $\partial_\eta g(x)=\varnothing$. When $g$ is finite-valued on a convex domain, $\partial g(x)$ agrees with [[def-subgradient-and-subdifferential]].”

def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn, Definition: “Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$. Its effective domain is $\operatorname{dom}g=\{x:g(x)<+\infty\}$. The function is **proper** if $\operatorname{dom}g\ne\varnothing$; it is **convex** if
$$g((1-\theta)x+\theta y)\le(1-\theta)g(x)+\theta g(y)\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^n,\ 0\le\theta\le1),$$
using the endpoint convention $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$ of [[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functionals-on-a-banach-space]]. It is **closed** (equivalently, lower semicontinuous in the extended-real convex-analysis convention used here) if its epigraph
$$\operatorname{epi}g=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:g(x)\le s\}$$
is closed in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$. The proximal-gradient items on this page assume $g$ is proper, closed and convex.”

def-proximal-mapping, Definition: “Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex, and let $t>0$. For $v\in\mathbb R^n$, define the set-valued proximal mapping
$$\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^n:g(u)+\frac{\|u-v\|_2^2}{2t}\le g(w)+\frac{\|w-v\|_2^2}{2t}\text{ for every }w\in\mathbb R^n\right\}.$$
The existence and uniqueness theorem on this page proves that this set is a singleton for every admissible $g,t,v$; its unique member is also denoted $\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)$.”

lem-proper-closed-convex-function-affine-minorant, Statement: “Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex in the epigraph convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. Then there are $a\in\mathbb R^n$ and $b\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$g(x)\ge\langle a,x\rangle+b\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^n).$$”

lem-smooth-composite-sum-preserves-proper-closed-convexity, Statement: “Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and convex, and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex under the epigraph convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. Then $F=f+g$ is proper, closed and convex in the same convention.”

thm-proximal-operator-existence-resolvent-firm-nonexpansive, Statement: “Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex in the epigraph convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. For every $t>0$ and $v\in\mathbb R^n$, the set $\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)$ is a singleton. Its unique element $u$ satisfies the resolvent equivalence
$$u=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (v-u)/t\in\partial g(u).$$
For any $v_1,v_2$ and $u_i=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v_i)$,
$$\|u_1-u_2\|_2^2\le\langle u_1-u_2,v_1-v_2\rangle.$$
In particular the proximal map is nonexpansive.”

required_interface.lasso-objective: Q_y(theta)=n^{-1}||y-X theta||_2^2+2 tau ||theta||_1 with tau>0 and no rank assumption.
required_interface.lasso-minimizer: the fixed-design Lasso minimizer set is nonempty, compact, and convex.
required_interface.soft-threshold: S_tau(t)=t-tau for t>tau, 0 for |t|<=tau, and t+tau for t<-tau.
required_interface.orthogonal-example: the existing orthogonal-design soft-threshold example remains canonical and is not duplicated.

suppliers.source_excerpt:
def-lasso-estimator, Definition: “For $n,d\ge1$, a deterministic design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, response $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and penalty $\tau>0$, define the Lasso objective
$$Q_y(\theta)=\frac1n\|y-X\theta\|_2^2+2\tau\|\theta\|_1.$$
Its minimizer set is $\mathcal M(y)=\operatorname{argmin}_{\theta\in\mathbb R^d}Q_y(\theta)$. The penalty is strictly positive; no full-rank condition on $X$ is imposed. The nonemptiness, compactness, and convexity of this set are proved separately; this page defines the objective and minimizer set but does not select one minimizer.”

lem-lasso-objective-has-minimizer, Statement: “Fix integers $n,d\ge1$, a deterministic matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, a response $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and a penalty $\tau>0$. The minimizer set $\mathcal M(y)$ of [[def-lasso-estimator]] is nonempty, compact, and convex.”

def-soft-thresholding-function, Definition: “For $\tau>0$ and $z\in\mathbb R$, define the **soft-thresholding map**
$$S_\tau(z)=\begin{cases}z-\tau,&z>\tau,\\0,&-\tau\le z\le\tau,\\z+\tau,&z<-\tau.\end{cases}$$”

ex-orthogonal-design-lasso-is-soft-thresholding, Example: “Let $n\ge d\ge1$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ satisfy $X^TX=nI_d$, and let $Y\in\mathbb R^n$ be any response. Set $Z=X^TY/n$ and use the penalty $\tau>0$ from [[def-lasso-estimator]]. The unique Lasso minimizer has coordinates $\widehat\theta_j=S_\tau(Z_j)$.”
